dictation.title: Dictation
dictation.subtitle: Talk instead of typing in any zerosoft field: hold {shortcut}, speak and let go. AI adds punctuation, drops filler words and applies your corrections.
dictation.noAi: AI cleanup is off, so only basic cleanup runs (filler words, corrections, punctuation and your dictionary).
dictation.hint: Anywhere in zerosoft: hold {shortcut} to dictate into the focused field, double tap it for hands-free and press Esc to cancel. A short tap still types the key as usual. Ctrl+Cmd+V on Mac, or Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V, pastes the last dictation.
dictation.rulesOnly: AI was not available: basic cleanup only.
dictation.rulesOff: Basic cleanup (AI cleanup is off in settings).
dictation.emptyBody: Hold {shortcut} in any text field. Every dictation lands here so you can copy it again.
dictation.deleteBody: It is removed from your history. Text you already pasted stays where it is.
dictation.learningOn: Fixing a dictation teaches your dictionary the corrected names and terms.
dictation.learningOff: Learning from corrections is off (Voice settings › Dictation).

dictation.aiCleanup: Clean up with AI (punctuation, filler words, corrections and lists)
dictation.stylesDesc: The same dictation reads differently in an email and in a chat. Voice picks the context from the app and the field.
dictation.commandMode: Command Mode: with text selected, say what to do with it

dictation.learnCorrections: Learn from my corrections: fixing a dictation in the history adds the corrected names and terms to the dictionary

dictionary.teamHelp: Team entries apply to everyone in the workspace; only admins add or remove them.

desktop.title: zerosoft for Mac and Windows
desktop.desc: The desktop app dictates into any app on your computer and records meetings with the system audio (Zoom, Meet, Teams or any call), without a bot.
desktop.unsigned: The builds are not signed yet. On Mac the first time, go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway (macOS 14 or earlier: right-click the app and choose Open); on Windows, click More info and Run anyway.
desktop.step1: Download the app for your computer from
desktop.step2: Open it and sign in with Google: the app opens your browser and comes back on its own.
desktop.step3: Hold Control + Option (Mac) or Ctrl + Windows (Windows) in any app to dictate. Meetings recorded there show up in Meetings.
desktop.whatDesc: It uses your zerosoft session, like this page.
desktop.what1: Hold-to-talk shortcut in any app: the clean text is pasted where the cursor is.
desktop.what2: Meeting notes with the system audio (macOS 13 or later and Windows) plus the microphone, from a calendar alert or when Zoom, Meet or Teams is in a call.
desktop.what3: Your dictionary and styles apply there too, because the cleanup runs on the server, and its dictations land in your history here.
desktop.mcpDesc: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client to your meetings. The key acts as you: it only sees your own meetings and dictations.
desktop.mcpStep1: Create an API key with the voice:read scope in
desktop.mcpStep2: Add this server to your MCP client:
desktop.mcpTools: Tools: list_meetings, get_meeting (notes and, if asked, the transcript), ask_meetings, list_dictations and list_folders.
desktop.webhooksDesc: voice.meeting.completed and voice.notes.ready reach only the webhooks and flows created by the person who recorded the meeting. Creating webhooks and flows is for admins, so a member’s meetings do not reach any webhook yet.

action_items.name: Action items
action_items.prompt: List every action item with its owner and due date, grouped by person. Say clearly when no owner or date was mentioned.

follow_up.name: Follow-up
follow_up.prompt: Write a short follow-up message for the other attendees: thanks, the key points, the decisions and the next steps with owners.

my_commitments.name: My commitments
my_commitments.prompt: What did I (Me) promise or agree to do? List each commitment with the date if one was said.

objections.name: Objections
objections.prompt: List the concerns or objections the other side raised and how each one was answered. Mark the ones left open.

coach.name: Coach me
coach.prompt: Give me honest feedback on how I ran this conversation: what went well, what to improve, and one thing to try next time. Quote short moments.

shorter.name: Shorter
shorter.prompt: Make it shorter and clearer. Keep every fact.

formal.name: More formal
formal.prompt: Rewrite it in a formal, polished tone for a work email.

friendly.name: Friendlier
friendly.prompt: Rewrite it in a warm, friendly tone, like a message to a colleague.

bullets.name: Bullet list
bullets.prompt: Turn it into a short bullet list, one idea per bullet.
